title: Employer Wage Reporting and Premiums Toolkit (v25.1, June 2026)
issuer: Washington Employment Security Department, Paid Family and Medical Leave

passages.question: The Q2 report as filed left out the June 26 bonus run. How is it corrected?
passages.excerpt: Report and premium payment due dates ... Q2: April, May, June July 31 Q3: July, August, September October 31 ... Amending a wage report will completely replace the previous report, so make sure it includes all the employees for that quarter, not just the employees that need adjustment. ... Starting August 1, 2026: A one percent (1%) monthly interest charge will be applied to overdue premium balances. Penalties will be assessed on late reports.

passages.question: Which of the quarter's wages carry each premium once the Paid Leave cap and the WA Cares exemptions are applied?
passages.excerpt: Paid Leave and WA Cares use the same definition of gross wages and hours. ... Once an employee meets the Social Security cap, you must stop withholding premiums on any additional wages over the cap but continue to report their wages. ... Stop deducting WA Cares premiums from the exempt worker beginning the effective date or the date they provided you notice, whichever is later. ... Employees with approved WA Cares exemptions must be included on quarterly wage reports and marked as exempt.
